chunks: And whatever is narrated from Abu Al-Jawzaʾ, I have narrated it from my father, and from Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan (may Allah be pleased with them both) from Saʿd ibn Abdullah, from Abu Al-Jawzaʾ Al-Munabbih ibn Abdullah. And I have also narrated it from Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan (may Allah be pleased with him) from Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan Al-Ṣaffar, from Abu Al-Jawzaʾ.

key_terms.الصَّفَّارِ: Al-Ṣaffar, an epithet meaning the goldsmith
key_terms.رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا: May Allah be pleased with them both (dual honorific)
key_terms.سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Saʿd ibn Abdullah, a key narrator

ai.seo_question: How is the transmission chain for Abu Al-Jawzaʾ verified in this hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq provides a rigorous biographical verification of the transmission chain for Abu Al-Jawzaʾ, a key narrator in Kufan hadith literature, by cross-referencing his personal recitations with those of his father and Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan. This dual attestation underscores the reliability of the Kufan scholarly network and highlights the meticulous attention to isnad integrity characteristic of early Shia hadith compilation. The clarification ensures that the narrations attributed to Abu Al-Jawzaʾ are firmly rooted in accepted scholarly lineages, reinforcing their authenticity for legal and theological derivation.
